mirror_norms.completeness_proof: Put pi=sqrt(2) and epsilon=1+pi. The coefficient epsilon is a unit and N(A15 D9) is even unimodular. For primitive r=(x,y), reflection integrality says q(r) divides 2I(r), I(r)=(epsilon*x,(y,N)). Away from (pi), local unimodularity and primitivity make I(r) the unit ideal. At (pi), a unit control gives v_pi(q)=0; otherwise a primitive spatial coordinate makes I(r) a unit, while evenness and q|2I force v_pi(q)=2. Every totally-positive unit of Z[sqrt(2)] is a square, so the complete canonical positive norms are 1 and 2.

outcome: No compact or finite-volume example in the certified prefix: the index-eight glue contributes nine non-root-lattice second-packet walls, eight coupling A15 to D9. The third packet adds 191 walls, 112 cross-component, but a strict D9-axis hyperideal ray survives all 208 positive-height walls.
